gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 11 build entry now keeps the existing gpio_wdt lane and the new bcm2835_wdt survey checkpoint reviewable together so the watchdog tranche does not drift across simple-driver anchors.
A dedicated survey gate makes the bcm2835_wdt gap explicit without pretending a Zig starter already exists, and it keeps the next bounded driver work tied to the live repo state.
The survey note records that Phase 11 now covers gpio_wdt with a landed starter while bcm2835_wdt still needs its first bounded scaffold, which keeps the roadmap gap honest inside the watchdog lane.

The next honest bcm2835_wdt step is a narrow starter around timeout tick encoding, running-bit detection, bounded start and stop transitions, restart intent, and poweroff-state bookkeeping before any MMIO-backed or platform-registered behavior.
Dedicated Phase 11 tests should arrive with the first starter so timeout tick conversion, restart intent, and poweroff-state bookkeeping stay reviewable without claiming hardware-backed execution.
A slice note would be useful once a real bcm2835_wdt starter exists, but writing it before the first Zig scaffold lands would turn survey language into fake product progress.

Probe-time details such as bootloader-carried running state, heartbeat and nowayout initialization, restart priority, and watchdog parent linkage should wait until the starter has the basic register-intent model in place.

Platform registration, PM base acquisition, the system power controller path, and poweroff handler coordination remain blocked until the lane has a small driver scaffold plus a hardware-validation matrix that can describe those side effects honestly.
